images.caption: Figure 1:Background and motivation.Agent performance depends on both the model and its harness, but task outcomes alone cannot distinguish model errors from harness shortfalls. TraceTrial-Bench uses native execution traces, artifacts, and environment state to assess agent performance and harness reliability separately and support evidence-based failure attribution.

Figure 2:TraceTrial-Bench overview.Mechanism-oriented tasks exercise native harnesses; trajectory tracing and multi-source evidence support separate Agent and Harness scores and evidence-based failure attribution. The figure’s evidence-extraction stage corresponds to the MEA module.

Figure 4:Taxonomy and task coverage of TraceTrial-Bench.(Left) Distribution of 40 mechanism-level reliability properties
across seven Harness components. The inner ring shows each
component’s share, and the outer ring lists individual properties,
with each property assigned equal weight.
(Right) Scope of each dimension and its task coverage in the
95-task evaluation population.

Figure 7:Admission and layered-evaluation order.Agent results are completed before Harness semantic judging, and the
two layers retain distinct evidence packets and verdict vectors.
